RQ01.note: the platform runs end to end on a real host and the scenario steps stand on passing evidence, except those the P12.01 matrix lists as partial or a gap: the signal-failure scenario is not implemented (D-01)

RQ02.note: one simulated edge site; the edge decides locally and buffers through an outage

RQ03.note: the central tier runs on the workstation and, deployed from the same manifests, on one real Ubuntu host; nothing runs on a remote cloud. Whether that satisfies the assessment is the assessor's decision (F-17).

RQ04.note: measured on one node of a shared host with synthetic events: clean to 312 events/s, a 30-minute soak, 56 native security checks

RQ05.note: the edge runtime is a non-root, read-only, capability-free container with resource limits, deployed in a Kubernetes cluster

RQ06.note: ONNX Runtime on CPU with one thread under 0.75 CPU and 512 MiB: warm inference p95 0.135 ms against a 100 ms target (LAT-01); the model beats the baseline on F1 with wide intervals (ACC-01)

RQ07.note: alerts, correlated incidents and bounded remediation with independent recovery verification; false incidents 29.6% against a 10% target (FA-03, F-08) and scale, failover and quarantine are plan-only (F-14)

RQ08.note: an editable source and an export exist from Phase 02; they are updated to the tested implementation and inspected in P13.01

RQ10.note: as RQ08; the proposed production views are separate and labelled not deployed (P13.02)

RQ12.note: the threat model covers every trust boundary; the diagram is updated in P13.01

RQ13.note: the placement decision is recorded with the deployed/proposed distinction; the proposed view is finished in P13.02

RQ14.note: the release, the publication review and the authorized push are P13.05-P13.07; the push is the user's

RQ15.note: the platform runs in a kind cluster (Kubernetes v1.36.4, the minor of the host's K3s) with Docker, deployed by a runbook that was followed as written; it is not deployed on K3s itself, which was proven feasible in P01.07

RQ16.note: Python with ONNX Runtime; the vision path is privacy-preserving feature aggregation, not OpenCV inference on video

RQ17.note: Mosquitto over mutual TLS at the edge and Redpanda (Kafka API) centrally

RQ18.note: Prometheus, Grafana, Tempo, Loki and OpenTelemetry on the workstation stack and on the target

RQ19.note: Keycloak (Authorization Code with PKCE), OPA, Trivy (scan of the shipped images) and Falco (on the target); service-to-service TLS and alert routing are open (F-12, F-13)

RQ20.note: a scoped mapping to GDPR, ISO 27001, IEC 62443, NIST CSF, ETSI EN 303 645, OWASP ASVS and AI frameworks with an explicit gap list; no compliance claim; eleven controls are partial (F-10)

RQ21.note: eight decision records exist; explaining and defending them is the student's, in P14

RQ22.note: configuration and deployment (a runbook followed as written), operation, failure and recovery (27 fault rows), scale (a measured ceiling) and security (56 native checks)

RQ23.note: the policies, roles, controls, risk register and DPIA-style review are written and checked against the code; the operational, security and privacy runbooks are exercised in P13.04

RQ24.note: the deck, its notes, PDF and rehearsal are P14.01-P14.03 and P14.09

RQ25.note: real-time processing, edge AI and the response to an event are evidenced for scenarios 1, 2, 3, 6 and 7 and in part for 4; scenario 5 is a gap (D-01); the live demonstration and its offline backup are P14.04

RQ26.note: the question bank and the mock interview are P14.05 and P14.09; the interview needs the student

RQ27.note: the M2, M3 and M4 walkthroughs and the live redesign need the student and cannot be done or inferred by an agent

RQ28.note: an AI-use statement and log for the student to own and defend is P14; AGENTS.md records that agents assist and labels every simulated or inferred value

RQ29.note: the rubric review and the rendered-deck inspection are P14.03

RQ30.note: at least ten structured questions are written in the P14.05 bank and rehearsed in P14.09
